Advances: ancora.tasks, ancora.gate

Findings: F6 (High, idioms H1 + api H1, consensus CF3; the preflight half F10 stays on ancora-90t). Consensus CF3 in ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-04/ancora-xla-post-ship-hardening/20260904-061300-consolidated.md.

Deliverable:
Five task moduledocs (lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:17, spec.validate.ex:16, spec.prime.ex:16, spec.status.ex:16, spec.review.ex:17) say `--spec-dir` "selects the subject directory. Defaults to `.spec/specs`." It selects the ancora workspace directory and defaults to `.spec`; Index derives `<spec_dir>/specs`. Passing the documented value: `mix spec.check --base HEAD --spec-dir .spec/specs` raises `** (RuntimeError) .spec/specs/specs directory not found` from Ancora.Index.detect_authored_dir/2 (index.ex:111-120), exits 1, prints no verdict line, which the read protocol in the same moduledoc defines as a crash. Output.classify/1 sorts it into the :internal tier where every other environment problem on this branch yields tier=env. test/mix/tasks/task_docs_test.exs:27 pins the presence of "Defaults to" and so guards text that is false; ancora.tasks.report_task_flags is a must.
Fix: correct the flag line in all five moduledocs (workspace directory, defaults to `.spec`); make Index.detect_authored_dir/2 and detect_spec_dir/1 (index.ex:57-59) return {:error, reason} so the gate and the other corpus-reading tasks route a bad or missing directory through gate_error/1 (or the task's fail path) as tier=env with a verdict line; extend task_docs_test.exs to assert the documented default VALUE equals the real default read from the task's option handling, not merely the phrase.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/mix/tasks/task_docs_test.exs, test/ancora/index_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_status_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate through the real tasks:
  1. `mix spec.check --base HEAD --spec-dir .spec/specs` ends `spec.check result=fail tier=env` with a message naming the directory it looked for and the flag's meaning, exit 1, no stack trace. Mutation: restore the raise in detect_authored_dir/2; the test must fail.
  2. `mix spec.status --spec-dir nope` (and validate) fail the same way with a verdict/usage line rather than a stack trace. Mutation: as above.
  3. The five moduledocs state the default `.spec` and the test compares that value against the real default. Mutation: change one moduledoc to `.spec/specs`; the test must fail.
  4. A correct `--spec-dir docs/spec` on a fixture whose corpus lives there still works for the tasks that already honor it (regression guard; preflight's own hardcode is ancora-90t and may still need a decoy `.spec/`; document that limit in the ticket record if it bites).
- Spec edit required in-diff: ancora.tasks (report_task_flags / check_flags) shall state the flag's meaning and default; ancora.gate (preflight_hard_fails or the env-tier statement) shall state that an unresolvable spec directory is an environment failure with a verdict line. Decision-record edit: affects entry or Consequences note on ancora.decision.cli_json_contract or ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: compile-graph-scoped checks only (`mix test --stale` or the named files) plus `mix spec.validate`; run `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` as a dev-loop check as soon as the spec edit exists, before either capped final-tier run.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, the named test files, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`, `mix spec.check --base e18fa05`, run-until-green. Full suite runs at the orchestrator's merge gate.
  - Verifier tier: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` plus targeted selections; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test that fails under the named mutation; prove each ordered test both ways and report the numbers
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh: the substantive requirement or scenario edit named below lands in the same diff with its decision-record edit; never a Spec-Ack trailer; never weaken a must
  - Fixtures never call production functions (use test/support or System.cmd); under file-scoped derivation a stray call binds a subject
  - Grader scratch discipline applies to you too: work only in this worktree, address it by absolute path
- Call-site Integration: Index.build/2 is called from Gate.check/2, Status, Next, Prime and Review; prove through the subprocess runs of at least spec.check and spec.status.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/gate/preflight.ex (ancora-90t: threading :spec_dir through preflight is a design decision between two conflicting musts)
- lib/ancora/review/**, lib/ancora/trailer.ex, lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/git/**, lib/ancora/derive/**, lib/ancora/config.ex
Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex, spec.validate.ex, spec.prime.ex, spec.status.ex, spec.review.ex, spec.next.ex (moduledoc flag lines and the error routing of an Index error only)
- lib/ancora/index.ex, lib/ancora/gate.ex (gate_error/1 and the Index.build call site only), lib/ancora/status.ex, lib/ancora/next.ex, lib/ancora/prime.ex (Index error rendering only)
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (substantive edits named above; never weakening a must)
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (binding-aware clause: derivation is file-scoped, so acknowledgment edits only, one substantive sentence describing what this ticket changed as that subject observes it, verified by execution; if the subject observes nothing, say so in the completion record and stop)
- .spec/decisions/** (every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; write a real contract statement, never a hollow line)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No new flag, no change to the eight-task count, no change to which directory is the default. Do not rebase; base stays e18fa05.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes (`mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass)
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

TEST_CRITIC: PASS

Ran the three touched files in the stage worktree (/Users/mz/src/ancora-41r.4): index_test + task_docs_test 10/10, spec_status_test 8/8, spec_check_test 22/22. No file edited. Below is a per-assertion verdict against what the ticket ordered, then the reachability limits and three warnings.

## Per-assertion verdict

1. test/ancora/index_test.exs "returns the requested workspace lookup failure as data"
   PASS. Pure, no subprocess, no corpus needed: Index.build(root, spec_dir: ".spec/specs") on an empty tmp root returns {:error, message} and both halves are asserted (the flag's meaning and ".spec/specs/specs directory not found"). This is the only assertion in the batch whose reachability reading can establish, since the value is returned in-process.

2. test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs "a requested subject directory is an environment failure"
   PASS on all three legs the ticket ordered. Exit status equality (status == 1), verdict-line EQUALITY on the last stdout line ("spec.check result=fail tier=env errors=0 warnings=0" via List.last(lines(stdout))), and a stack-trace refute. Message asserted on stdout before the verdict. See warning W1 on the refute's narrowness.

3. test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs "tasks read a corpus from a non-default workspace"
   PASS, unevenly. All five tasks are driven with --spec-dir docs/spec against a fixture whose only subject lives there, each asserting exit 0 and refute stderr =~ "** (". For spec.check, spec.validate and spec.status the assertion is "checked subjects=1" / "subjects=1", which does prove the subject only present under docs/spec was found. For spec.prime the assertion is "Spec Led Prime" (a banner) and for spec.review "spec.review wrote" (a completion line); neither names the corpus. Those two lean entirely on exit 0 as the discriminator, which does hold here: the fixture's .spec/ has no specs/ subdirectory, so a task that ignored the flag would fail its authored-dir resolution and exit non-zero. It works, but it is indirect. Recommend asserting a subject count or the subject id for prime and review too. See warning W2 on the decoy.

4. test/mix/tasks/spec_status_test.exs "status routes an invalid workspace without a stack trace"
   PASS. Exit 1, the flag's meaning and "nope/specs directory not found" on stdout, refute stdout =~ "result=", refute stderr =~ "** (RuntimeError)". No verdict-line equality leg, and that is CORRECT rather than a gap: spec.status emits no verdict, which four pre-existing tests in the same file already pin. The load-bearing guards here are the stdout message and the exit status.

5. test/mix/tasks/spec_status_test.exs "validate routes an invalid workspace without a stack trace"
   PASS on all three legs. Exit 1, verdict-line EQUALITY ("spec.validate result=fail tier=env errors=0 warnings=0"), stack-trace refute, plus both halves of the message.

6. test/mix/tasks/spec_status_test.exs "review routes an invalid workspace without a stack trace"
   PASS but UNDER-ASSERTED. It checks exit 1, "nope/specs directory not found", refute result=, refute RuntimeError, but it does NOT assert the flag-meaning clause ("--spec-dir selects the ancora workspace directory") that the ticket ordered for every task and that the other three tests do assert. The string is emitted (same Index.detect_authored_dir message), so this is an assertion gap, not a behavior gap. Also the tag is spec: "ancora.review.meta_line_shape", which is about the review artifact's meta line, not env routing; the parallel status and validate tests are tagged ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails + ancora.tasks.gated_emission_paths, which is the fitting pair.

7. test/mix/tasks/task_docs_test.exs "spec-dir help names the workspace and matches the real default"
   PASS, and it answers the review's H2 correctly. The comparison value is derived, not hand-written: Ancora.Index.detect_spec_dir(File.cwd!()) is the SAME function each of the five tasks calls when --spec-dir is absent (spec.validate.ex:48, spec.review.ex:71, and via Index.resolve_spec_dir / Status.spec_dir for the rest). A second literal map would have gone stale; this cannot. See warning W3 for what it still does not bind.

## Weakening of existing tests

The commit deletes spec_check_test's "internal exception has no verdict on stdout", which rm'd .spec/specs to force a raise. That scenario is now an env failure by design, so the deletion is justified rather than a dodge. The contract it guarded survives at the unit level in test/ancora/output_test.exs:129-164 ("internal re-raises with no verdict line" and the {:internal, %RuntimeError{}} tuple case). Net effect worth naming: there is no longer any SUBPROCESS-level proof that the internal tier prints no verdict; grep finds :internal only in output_test.exs. I do not consider that blocking, because no easy CLI path reaches the internal tier any more, but it is a real reduction and the reason the deletion is not free.

No other existing assertion was changed or relaxed. The pre-existing blanket `assert moduledoc =~ "Defaults to"` is untouched; it is no longer the only guard for --spec-dir (finding 7 supersedes it there), but it remains the only guard for every other flag's documented default, e.g. --base and --output.

## Assertions pinning source text rather than behavior

Only one, and defensibly: the docs test's regex pins the exact moduledoc sentence "`--spec-dir DIR` selects the ancora workspace directory. Defaults to `X`." A correct-but-reworded moduledoc fails it. That is the nature of a docs contract and the ticket ordered the wording, so I am not flagging it. Note it is a doc-phrasing coupling for future editors. The CI-workflow test in the same file already pins workflow text; unchanged by this commit.

## UNVERIFIED BY READING: needs the mutation run

Reading establishes what these assertions name, not that they are REACHABLE, because every one of them depends on subprocess stdout/stderr delivery through run_mix_subprocess.

- M1 (the important one). In lib/ancora/index.ex restore detect_authored_dir to `raise "#{authored} directory not found in #{root}."` and drop the {:spec_dir, message} clause in gate_error. Re-run spec_check_test and spec_status_test. All four env tests must fail, and at least one must fail ON the `refute stderr =~ "** (RuntimeError)"` line specifically. If the earlier asserts always trip first, the stack-trace guard is decorative and has never been exercised, which matters because it is the ticket's third leg.
- M2. Change one of the five moduledocs to "Defaults to `.spec/specs`." The docs test must fail for that module only.
- M3. Strip :spec_dir from one task's parsed opts (spec.prime is the cleanest) so it falls back to .spec. "tasks read a corpus from a non-default workspace" must fail on that invocation. This is what proves the prime/review legs of finding 3 are discriminators rather than smoke.

## Warnings (none blocking)

W1. The stack-trace guard is exception-class specific in all four env tests: `refute stderr =~ "** (RuntimeError)"`. A regression that surfaces as MatchError, CaseClauseError, FunctionClauseError or `** (Mix)` passes it. The spec scenario language at .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md:292 says "stderr contains no internal exception", and the non-default-workspace test in the same commit already uses the broader `refute stderr =~ "** ("`. Recommend the broad form in all four for consistency with both the spec and the sibling test.

W2. The decoy is hidden. create_custom_spec_project writes ".spec/.keep" => "" with no comment. That empty directory exists solely to get past the ancora-90t preflight bug (Gate.Preflight.corpus hardcodes File.dir?(root <> "/.spec") regardless of --spec-dir), which is exactly the workaround ancora-90t's own report describes two earlier agents having to invent. Undocumented, it reads as incidental fixture noise; when ancora-90t is fixed nobody will know it can go. Recommend a one-line comment in the fixture naming ancora-90t.

W3. The docs test binds to Index.detect_spec_dir but not to the other literal. lib/ancora/gate.ex:89 and :113 both carry `Keyword.get(opts, :spec_dir) || ".spec"`. Change that literal and the docs plus the docs test would still agree while gate behavior diverged. Minor, since detect_spec_dir covers the fallback the moduledocs actually describe. Second, smaller point: the test's `assert {:ok, default_spec_dir} = detect_spec_dir(File.cwd!())` depends on the ancora repo itself having a .spec/ directory; in a checkout without one the test fails on the match instead of checking the docs. Always true here, so it is a note.

## One gap the ticket did not order

spec.prime accepts --spec-dir and has no env-routing test. I checked it live rather than guessing: Ancora.Prime.build(root, spec_dir: "nope") returns {:env, "could not derive status: \"--spec-dir selects the ancora workspace directory; nope/specs directory not found in ...\""}. So the behavior is correct and prime is not a hole, but its message is double-wrapped and quote-escaped where the other four are clean. Out of scope for this ticket; worth a follow-up if the wrapping bothers anyone.
